import pandas as pd

def main():
    # Source file path
    source0_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length1_48/test_0.csv"
    # Target output path
    target_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length1_48/target_multisource_cot.csv"

    # Load source data
    df0 = pd.read_csv(source0_path)

    # Inspect columns of source0:
    # ['Text Date', 'Value Date', 'Zip Code', 'Water Use', 'Power Use']

    # Transformation plan:
    # - Target schema: ['Date': string, 'Water Use': float, 'Power Use': integer]
    # - Source0 has 'Text Date' which matches the target 'Date' format (e.g. Apr_2007)
    # - Aggregate by 'Text Date' to get total Water Use (sum) and total Power Use (sum)
    #   because target examples show aggregated values per Date (not per Zip Code)
    # - Convert Power Use to integer (sum will be float by default)
    # - Water Use keep as float

    # Group by 'Text Date' and aggregate sums
    grouped = df0.groupby('Text Date', as_index=False).agg({
        'Water Use': 'sum',
        'Power Use': 'sum'
    })

    # Rename 'Text Date' to 'Date'
    grouped.rename(columns={'Text Date': 'Date'}, inplace=True)

    # Convert Power Use to integer
    grouped['Power Use'] = grouped['Power Use'].round().astype(int)

    # Reorder columns to match target schema exactly
    grouped = grouped[['Date', 'Water Use', 'Power Use']]

    # Save to target CSV
    grouped.to_csv(target_path, index=False)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
